title: Integrative structural glycobiology: From molecular recognition to dynamic multivalent assemblies.
one_liner_zh: 该综述聚焦蛋白质-糖识别中的结构糖生物学，强调结合实验与计算建模解析动态多价组装，虽以糖类为对象但结构建模思路可迁移至蛋白质体系。
abstract: Protein-carbohydrate recognition plays an important role in structural biology. Glycans store molecular information through their monosaccharide makeup, stereochemistry, linkage positions, branching, substitutions, and three-dimensional shapes. Glycans are often flexible and structurally diverse, and their interactions are typically individually weak. As a result, glycan recognition in biology usually cannot be described as a single, static ligand fitting into a protein binding pocket. Instead, it depends on a mix of factors, including glycan shape, protein structure, hydration, electrostatic forces, molecular movement, context, density, and multivalency. These factors have led structural glycobiology to shift from focusing only on isolated high-resolution structures to using both experimental and computational data to build models that span different spaces and times. This review examines the main ideas behind this shift. It highlights what makes carbohydrate recognition different from other ligand-protein interactions. It offers a practical, evidence-based way to interpret structural models.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质-碳水化合物识别在结构生物学中扮演重要角色。聚糖通过其单糖组成、立体化学、连接位置、分支、取代基及三维形状存储分子信息。聚糖通常具有柔性和结构多样性，其相互作用通常各自较弱。因此，生物学中的聚糖识别通常不能描述为单个静态配体嵌入蛋白质结合口袋。相反，它依赖于多种因素的综合作用，包括聚糖形状、蛋白质结构、水合作用、静电力、分子运动、环境、密度和多价性。这些因素促使结构糖生物学从仅关注孤立的高分辨率结构，转向利用实验和计算数据构建跨越不同空间和时间的模型。本综述探讨了这一转变背后的主要理念，强调碳水化合物识别与其他配体-蛋白质相互作用的不同之处，并提供了一种基于证据的实用方法来解读结构模型。
